diagnosis: JavaScript Array.prototype.sort() sorts elements lexicographically by default (converting numbers to strings, e.g. [10, 2] becomes [10, 2]).
rule: ALWAYS pass a numeric comparator: arr.sort((a, b) => a - b). For descending sort: arr.sort((a, b) => b - a).

verdict: Runtime Error (Maximum call stack size exceeded)
diagnosis: Node.js default V8 call stack is limited to ~10,000 frames. Deep recursion in DFS on trees or graphs where N can reach 2e5 causes immediate crash.
rule: ALWAYS replace deep recursive DFS with an explicit iterative stack array (const stack = [start]) or iterative BFS queue.

diagnosis: Allocating fixed-size MAX arrays (e.g. new Array(200005)) inside while(t--) loop triggers excessive GC pause times across hundreds of test cases.
rule: Allocate arrays dynamically sized to current n (new Int32Array(n)), or allocate a single static global buffer once outside the testcase loop.

diagnosis: In JavaScript, negative numbers preserve sign under remainder operator (%): (-5) % 3 === -2. This breaks modular arithmetic invariants.
rule: Always compute modular arithmetic with non-negative guarantee: ((val % MOD) + MOD) % MOD.

diagnosis: Using BigInt for standard 32-bit or 53-bit integers is 3x to 5x slower than native Number arithmetic, causing avoidable TLE.
rule: Use native Number up to 9e15 (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 9007199254740991). Only switch to BigInt when numbers provably exceed 9e15 (such as 10^18 products).
